title: REST vs. GraphQL, gRPC, WebSockets, SSE and webhooks
summary: REST is the standard for public resource APIs.

sections.definition: REST is the standard for public resource APIs. GraphQL lets the client ask for exactly the fields it needs. gRPC is fast binary RPC between services. WebSockets give persistent bidirectional communication, SSE is a stream from the server to the client, and webhooks are HTTP requests that someone else’s server sends you when an event happens.
sections.analogy: REST: a restaurant with a fixed menu. GraphQL: a buffet where you build your plate. gRPC: the internal communication between kitchen and bar with short codes. WebSocket: an open phone call. SSE: the radio, you only listen. Webhook: "we will call you when your table is ready".
sections.problem: Choosing badly is costly: GraphQL in a simple public API adds complexity (hard HTTP caching, expensive queries); polling every second instead of SSE wastes resources; WebSockets for something that flows in only one direction complicates scaling; and not verifying a webhook’s signature lets anyone mark orders as paid.
sections.code:wire:
# GraphQL: un endpoint, el cliente elige los campos
POST /graphql
{"query":"{ pedido(id:1093){ total cliente{ nombre } } }"}

# SSE: una respuesta que no termina
GET /v1/pedidos/1093/eventos
Accept: text/event-stream
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: text/event-stream

event: estado
data: {"estado":"en_preparacion"}

event: estado
data: {"estado":"enviado"}

# Webhook: la pasarela de pagos llama a TU API
POST https://api.tienda.co/v1/webhooks/pagos
X-Signature: t=1731456000,v1=5257a869e7...
{"evento":"pago.aprobado","pago_id":"pay_501"}
sections.code:server:
from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

@app.get("/v1/pedidos/{id}/eventos")
async def eventos(id: int):
    async def stream():
        async for estado in escuchar_cambios(id):
            yield f"event: estado\ndata: {estado}\n\n"
    return StreamingResponse(stream(), media_type="text/event-stream")

@app.websocket("/ws/soporte")
async def chat(ws: WebSocket):
    await ws.accept()
    while True:
        msg = await ws.receive_text()
        await ws.send_text(f"Agente: recibido '{msg}'")
sections.bridge:typescript: You already know the client side of almost all of them: Apollo for GraphQL, new WebSocket(), new EventSource() for SSE, which is exactly what AI chat interfaces use to show the answer token by token. Webhooks have no frontend side: they are server to server.
sections.interview: REST is my default option for resource APIs, especially public ones, for its simplicity, HTTP caching and ecosystem. I consider GraphQL when there are many clients with very different data needs and I want to avoid fetching too much data or making several calls, accepting more complexity in caching, per-field authorization and query cost control. I use gRPC between internal microservices for performance and typed contracts with Protocol Buffers. WebSockets for real-time bidirectional communication, like chat. SSE when only the server sends updates, like progress or AI streaming. And webhooks to notify events to other systems, always signed and processed idempotently.
sections.myths:
• Believing GraphQL replaces REST. It solves other problems: many clients with different data needs.
  • Thinking gRPC works directly from the browser. It needs gRPC-Web and a proxy.
  • Using WebSockets for one-way notifications when SSE is enough.
